the role of nasal allergy on the development of otitis media with effusion (OME).
the role of the nose in the development and persistence of otitis media.
the relationship between the presence of OME and the presence of allergic rhinitis, and the effect of the latter on the former.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the role of nasal allergy is not clear, however, it may play a role in the development of OME.
the role of allergy in otitis media with effusion is not well established.
the presence of nasal allergies is a significant risk factor in the pathogenesis of otitis media with effusion in children.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is no evidence that allergy has an impact on the incidence of acute otitis media or otitis media with effusion.
we have shown that the nasal allergic response is a major contributor to Otitis Media in children and adults.
the use of nasal allergy in children with otitis media with effusion (OME) is a significant factor that can affect the severity of the condition and the response to treatment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
nasal allergies are a common cause of OME in children.
nasal allergy may be a risk factor for OME, and the risk increases with the severity of the allergic rhinitis, as assessed by the ARIA criteria.
the presence of allergy is a major factor contributing to OME, and the treatment of allergy may help in the management of OME.
